en: Śrīḥ!

The Tithi-nirṇaya, which is among all the fundamental works composed by the venerable Ānandatīrtha Bhāgavata. Salutations to Śrī Lakṣmī-Hayagrīva, who is identical with Śrī Hanumat, Bhīma, Madhva, Antargada Rāma, Kṛṣṇa, and Vedavyāsa.
Having bowed to Viṣṇu, the Lord of the Universe, for the sake of purification through fasting upon Him,
this determination of the lunar day (tithi) is composed in accordance with the original text.
From the year Kali 4100 onwards, the venerable Bhūśrībhinna Ācārya,
having abandoned the solar [cult] which yields fruitless results, attained the speech of the one to be meditated upon as Garuḍa.

One should make the first part from the zodiac sign (rāśi) and the middle part from the "cow-slayer" (goghna); having subtracted the digits (kalās) from the "son of wisdom" (buddhi), one should establish the fixed point (dhruva) as the worshipper of Hara, supported by the region.
From Anantavṛddha, [the lineage reached] Baudhāṅga; from him, equal to him, came Indu, multiplied by Śuka, diminished by Prājña, Añjalibhṛt, Āpta, Nasta, Tāra, Śobha, and Atinākin.
From the days, having obtained the passion of passion from the lunar [calculation], it should be diminished by one day;
then, subtracting the parts obtained from Jagatsena’s limbs, the excellent and inconceivable [result] is for worship with water.

The minutes of arc resulting from the middle correction of the planets at the eastern and western locations relative to the meridian line passing through Laṅkā and other points are respectively negative and positive. (6)
The minutes obtained from the sun by multiplying the number of elapsed days by twelve and subtracting them from the sine of the sun's diameter;
the resulting arc is equal to that [correction] applied to the sun. (7)

From the arc-dorjya-phala subtracted [from the sun], as it was from the sun, so too from that phala, by means of the "cow-slayer" (goghna), "divine" (divya), and "progeny" (prajā) [coefficients], the minutes of arc for sandalwood and lotus are obtained. (8)
For the purification of the country and the arms, there would be viliptikās in the [measure] of the giver’s strength;
the Sun’s [ascendant] is fixed as the sign of the female portion that has been observed. (9)

One who nourishes the body, whose mind is a dwelling place, who is somehow not born from a lotus, who is skilled in honor, a home for parrots, free from disease, a traveler on the path of wisdom, a man of intellect, devoted to sleep, and a sovereign of the arts—such is the wise man. 10.
Mahāśara, Dūrasara, Dhamīhari, Hasandhura, Vedanaga, Susaṅkula;
Tamaḥkhaga, Pārabala, Rasābala, Dhanāvali, Kārabhṛgu, and Jagadbhaga. || 11 ||
These twenty-four sines are for the sake of the accuracy of the sun and moon; they know these to be the twenty-four statements concerning the three signs. (12)
If half the bowstring is not completed by the measurement of the auspicious limb, then, having subtracted the current sine, there is the collection of the results for the Murāru [Viṣṇu]. (13)
In the case of two [distances] of four *yojanas* or two *pādas*, the wise call the past and future portions the "arm" (*bhuja*). (14)
The sine of the Sun’s longitude and the sine of the Moon’s longitude are increased by six and nine [respectively] in sequence;
these, divided by sixty, become minutes [of correction], which are positive or negative according to their respective spheres (gola). || 15 ||
The minutes of arc traversed by the planets in one day are their respective daily motions.

The mass of kalpa-years multiplied by the number of cows (sixty) and added to the solar [years] with their fruitless results—[from this total], the quotient obtained by dividing by the measure of months is called the precession (*ayanam*) in signs and so forth. (16)

It is a jewel of light, a purifier of the intellect, the locus of song, and the fuel for all beings; it is the eternal body, full of bliss, worthy of being beheld, and possesses a form like lightning.
The words "navabhāryā" refer to the knower who removes the infinite seasons;
having added the minutes of arc of the sine of that arm to the sun, one should then subtract them according to the two spheres.
The [planets] smeared with the arms mentioned in the verses beginning with "arkapūjya" are said to be in motion;
the Sun is to be worshipped, the Moon is the maker of nectar, and the Lord is praised as the one who sports in passion. 19.
"Alaṅ-kṛṣṇo," "hitoddeśo," "gatibhūto," "smarājito," "śaśidhātā"—these are the words; here, however, the one who knows the end is the "hāraka. (20)
The minutes of arc for the daily motion of the planets are derived from their respective daily movements;
these are multiplied by the half-ascensional difference (carārdha) and divided by ninety-six (anantāṅga).
These minutes are subtracted at sunrise and added at sunset, and the reverse occurs when the planet is in the northern or southern hemisphere respectively.
The correction for the longitudinal difference (deśāntara) and the correction for the difference in latitudes (dordvivara) are prescribed in the middle [of the calculation];
whereas the correction for the ascensional difference (caradala) is performed by the wise immediately after the computation of the true [longitude]. || 22 ||
One should subtract the number of days from the previously mentioned corrected moon;
the remainder, when divided by sixty *ghaṭīs*, gives the elapsed lunar day (*tithi*) as the quotient. || 23 ||
One should divide the current [value] by twelve liptās to obtain the tithi;
the quotient is to be known as nāḍikās, while the remainder is proclaimed as liptās. || 24 ||

If there is an increase of more than twelve [nāḍīs], it is one; if there is an increase, however, it is sixteen. In the case of equality, it is two or one *kalā*; in the case of decrease, this is four or more. (25)

If [the additive] is greater than eight, it is subtracted from sixteen; if it is eight, it is subtracted from eight; if it is equal [to eight], four; if it is less than eight, two, one, or zero, respectively.
In the case of subtraction, this [process] is applied starting from four.
According to the Vārāha [Purāṇa], the new moon (darśā) and the full moon (paurṇamāsī) that do not extend across midday are prescribed;
however, the Śroṇā [tithi] that does not extend beyond midday should be observed as a fast by those devoted to Viṣṇu. 27.
One who desires the fruit of fasting should abstain from four meals;
however, during the first and last watches of the day, one may eat at sunset, while during the middle watch, one must fast.
Having observed that the twelfth lunar day (dvādaśī) extends for half a *kalā* beyond midnight,
all ritual acts (*kriyā*) up until midday must be performed, according to the command of Śambhu.
Thus ends the *Tithinirṇaya* (The Determination of Lunar Days) composed by the venerable Ānandatīrtha Bhagavatpāda.
